title: Swarm Robotics Formation Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates a swarm of 12 small robots on a flat ground plane, capable of switching between different geometric formations under user control.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 25, 30) looking at the origin.
- Add a large flat plane (60x60) at y=0 with a dark gray grid material or subtle grid lines to represent the arena floor.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light from (10, 20, 10) with intensity 0.8.
- Create 12 robot agents as small box meshes (size ~0.8x0.5x0.8) with a distinct color (e.g., cyan 0x00ccff). Each robot should have a small cone or arrow mesh on top indicating its heading direction.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Robots start scattered randomly within a 10-unit radius circle around the origin at y=0.25.

FORMATIONS:
- Support 4 formations: 'circle' (radius 8), 'line' (horizontal line along x-axis, spacing 2.5), 'grid' (3 rows x 4 columns, spacing 3), 'vee' (V-shape pointing forward along +z, angle 45 degrees, spacing 2.5 along each arm).
- Default formation on load: 'none' (robots stay at random initial positions).

ROBOT MOVEMENT BEHAVIOR:
- When a formation is selected, each robot is assigned a unique target position in that formation.
- Robots move toward their target using a simple steering behavior: velocity = normalize(target - position) * speed. Use speed = 4 units/sec.
- Robots decelerate smoothly when within 1.0 unit of their target (linearly scale speed by distance/1.0).
- A robot is considered 'arrived' when it is within 0.15 units of its target.
- Robots should rotate (yaw around Y axis) to face their movement direction.
- Implement basic collision avoidance: if two robots are within 1.2 units of each other, apply a small repulsion force (magnitude 2.0) pushing them apart.

SPEED CONTROL:
- A slider input (range 1 to 10, default 4, step 0.5) labeled 'Speed' controls the base movement speed of all robots.

UI / HUD:
- Place 4 buttons at the top of the screen labeled: 'Circle', 'Line', 'Grid', 'V-Shape'.
- Style buttons with dark background, white text, padding 8px 16px, margin 4px, cursor pointer. Highlight the active formation button with a bright border (e.g., 2px solid #00ccff).
- Display a HUD overlay (top-left, semi-transparent dark background) showing:
  - Current formation name
  - Number of robots arrived at target (e.g., 'Arrived: 7/12')
  - Average distance to targets (2 decimal places)
  - Simulation time in seconds (1 decimal place)
- Place the speed slider below the formation buttons.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields updated every frame:
  - robotCount: number (always 12)
  - currentFormation: string ('none', 'circle', 'line', 'grid', 'vee')
  - arrivedCount: number (robots within 0.15 of target)
  - averageDistance: number (mean distance of all robots to their assigned targets, 0 if no formation)
  - simTime: number (elapsed simulation time in seconds)
  - speed: number (current speed setting from slider)
  - robotPositions: array of {x, y, z} for each robot
  - targetPositions: array of {x, y, z} for each robot's current target (empty array if formation is 'none')
  - formationComplete: boolean (true if all 12 robots have arrived)
  - collisionAvoidanceActive: boolean (true if any pair of robots is currently within 1.2 units)

ANIMATION:
- Use requestAnimationFrame with a proper delta-time clock.
- Robots should animate smoothly toward targets.
- The heading indicator (cone/arrow) should rotate to match movement direction.

IMPORTANT: Initialize window.__3D_STATE__ before the first frame renders. All numerical values must be NaN-free (default to 0).
physics_constraints: Robots must stay on the ground plane (y=0.25 constant). Collision avoidance repulsion must prevent overlapping (no two robots closer than ~0.8 units center-to-center during steady state). Speed scales linearly with the slider value. Deceleration zone is 1.0 unit from target. Arrival threshold is 0.15 units.
